title: Crosslane memory-merge prefill scheduler to reduce host copy and thread contention
creator: Miguel Reyes
description: Background: We continue to see 10-25% tail latency variance on small-message prefill workloads attributed to frequent short DMA/memcpy operations and threadpool wakeups on the host. Previous work reduced large-copy spikes, but micro-copy fanout and scheduling churn remain. Goal: implement a crosslane memory-merge layer in the host prefill pipeline that coalesces small contiguous staging buffers into larger contiguous transfers, amortizes locks, and introduces a lightweight descheduler to reduce threadpool wakeups during bursty prefill phases. Scope includes scheduler hooks for kernel-selection hints (to prefer attention-optimized kernels when long-sequence prefill is detected), single-hop aggregated memcpy submission to the DMA engine, and a fairness window to prevent starvation of low-priority requests.
acceptance_criteria: P50 latency for 1-4 token prefill workloads improves by >= 15% in synthetic burst test
95th percentile end-to-end prefill + first-decode latency reduced by >= 12% on representative customer traces
Host CPU utilization during 500 qps burst decreases by >= 20% while GPU utilization is unchanged or improved
No regressions in correctness: KV cache integrity and sequence order preserved (validated by regression harness)
New scheduler feature guarded by feature-flag and default-off for dedicated customers until rollout complete
implementation_notes: Design: add a CrosslaneMerger component in the host prefill stage that maintains per-GPU 'lane' ring metadata and a short coalesce window (configurable, default 1ms). The merger aggregates contiguous staging regions into a single pinned buffer and submits one DMA operation per merged group. Integrate with existing token-aware batching so coalescing respects model sequence boundaries. Introduce a lightweight 'deschedule' token for worker threads: after submitting a merged DMA, workers yield to a pooled completion thread to avoid thundering wakes. Add kernel-selection hinting API (KernelHint::PREFILL_LONGSEQ) upstream so runtime can prefer attention-optimized kernels when merged groups predict long subsequent sequences.

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Merging across logical lanes could violate per-request ordering if not careful. Mitigation: track sequence ids and only merge contiguous sequence ranges; fall back to per-request copies when out-of-order gaps detected. Risk: larger DMA submits could increase backpressure on GPU if not paced; mitigation: integrate with token-aware batching so merged submits are throttled to match expected decode throughput.
